technical_facts: Implemented a custom BSP portalization process that was 20% faster and used 1/5 the memory.
Developed 'QuakeWorld' specifically for internet play, moving from a game-style loop to a fileserver/database style loop to reduce latency.
Introduced client-side movement simulation in QuakeWorld to guess results of user movement before receiving authoritative server responses.
Rewrote sound loading and mixing to fix refcounting and hanging bugs.
Developed a radiosity replacement for lighting Quake maps, allowing textures to be tagged as light emitters.
Ported Quake to OpenGL and Win32, advocating for OpenGL over Direct-3D due to its procedural interface and ease of use.
Optimized qcc compiler by moving defs to the head of the search list, resulting in a 4x speed increase.
Implemented a master server system for QuakeWorld to handle server registration and global rankings.
Changed edicts from indexes to pointers to optimize entity management.
Utilized a blend pass to implement light maps in GLQuake, which is fill-rate intensive.
Implemented IP packet filtering and user ID filtering for server administration in QuakeWorld.
personality_patterns: Extreme focus on technical efficiency and performance optimization.
Pragmatic approach to architecture ('practical above idealistic').
Willingness to admit technical mistakes ('Ok, I made a bad call') and pivot quickly.
Direct and blunt communication style, especially regarding technical tools and APIs (e.g., his critique of Direct-3D).
High work ethic and tendency to ignore personal time ('Vacation? I don't need a vacation!').
Strong preference for clean, readable, and procedural code over complex, boilerplate-heavy APIs.

gnosis_principles.description: Moving from a synchronous game loop (fetch-process-send) to an asynchronous, packet-driven model (process each packet as it arrives) drastically reduces response time.
Allowing the client to simulate physics locally to provide immediate feedback, while treating the server as the final authority to correct mispredictions.
An API that is painful to use (like Direct-3D Immediate Mode's COM/execute buffers) slows down development, increases bugs, and hinders the exploration of new algorithmic improvements.
Identifying the most basic primitive (e.g., switching from reliable streams to unreliable packets as the core network primitive) simplifies the rest of the system.

heritage_patterns: The use of a master server for global matchmaking and ranking.
The implementation of 'hunks' for memory management and allocation.
The pattern of using .plan files for transparent, daily technical logging and project tracking.
The approach of porting a core engine to multiple APIs (OpenGL, D3D, software) to benchmark performance and developer experience.

dpo_pairs.prompt: Why did John Carmack prefer OpenGL over Direct-3D for Quake?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He found OpenGL's procedural interface much easier to use and more efficient for development, whereas Direct-3D Immediate Mode required complex COM routines and execute buffers that made the code verbose and painful to write.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He simply liked the graphics quality of OpenGL better than Direct-3D.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What was the primary technical change in QuakeWorld to improve internet play?
dpo_pairs.chosen: The server model was changed from a game-style loop to a fileserver/database style loop, processing packets as they arrived rather than in a fixed frame cycle, which reduced response time from over 50ms to under 4ms.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He increased the bandwidth of the servers to allow more players to connect simultaneously.

dpo_pairs.prompt: What did Carmack learn about client-side prediction in QuakeWorld?
dpo_pairs.chosen: He found that while it smoothed out motion, simulating too much (like projectiles) created discrepancies between the client and server that were too disruptive for a twitch-reaction game.
dpo_pairs.rejected: He discovered that client-side prediction was completely useless and removed it entirely from the game.
